# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.32 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.31. Written and tried by the author's assistant on one Linux machine. The automated test suite passes on CI runners for Linux x86-64 and arm64, Windows x86-64 and arm64, and macOS (Apple silicon and Intel). **Nothing was tried by hand on Windows, macOS or arm64, and no photo batch was processed there.**

**New**
- **`--scan-escl`**: scan from a network scanner over eSCL/AirScan (plain HTTP, JPEG).
- **`--apply-text FILE`**: put a hand-corrected text back onto the recognised words, so the PDF text layer, `--txt` and hOCR carry the corrections.
- **Proofreading window (GUI)**: page picture beside the editable text, list of doubtful words from hOCR with a crop and an outlined box, loading of the last export, and export of a PDF with the corrections.

**Better**
- **`--quality-report`**: false "looks like duplicate" notes 124 -> 0 and false "text may be cut off" notes 29 -> 1 on six real magazine issues (248 pages); a really repeated page is still found.
- **Native engine layout**: text above a column that could not be cut, and a heading set larger than the body, are now recovered (one page 53 -> 116 words; three pages changed over the six issues, none worse).

**Verified**: unit tests and clippy; CI on all jobs; `--apply-text` on three real pages (unchanged text gives 0 changes and a byte-identical `--txt`; three corrected words reach PDF, txt and hOCR).
**Not verified**: eSCL on a real scanner (only a mock server); the **Dockerfile was never built as an image**; the window's buttons and file dialogs were not clicked; `--apply-text` on whole books or split double sheets; character error rate (no hand-checked text); the GUI on Windows, macOS and arm64; the winget manifest (still pre.28, not validated).

**Known limits**: a large italic heading on a dotted ground can still be misread (one title read "Drapii nostri"); the doubtful-word list is noisy with Tesseract confidences; text cut at the edge is found on 29 of 40 test crops; photos that are not pages are kept; tables and contents pages read few words; OCR can misread characters such as `@`.
